To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce a new model architecture, Sparse Transformer, that is able to model long sequences by using sparse factorizations of attention matrices.

we have developed a new sparse attention mechanism, which allows us to train very deep transformer networks, and that these networks can be trained on a wide variety of tasks, achieving new state-of-the-art results on all of them.

(i) sparse factorizations of attention matrices can be used to model long sequences with Transformers; (ii) sparse factorizations are compatible with the use of deep networks; (iii) the use of recomputed attention matrices can reduce memory requirements for training; and (iv) fast attention kernels can improve training.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a) the use of sparsity to scale attention to very long sequences; b) a new initialization method and architecture for deep networks that are harder to train, but can train deeper; c) a new way of using attention to compress raw bytes into a representation that can be modeled with a dense layer, allowing us to model raw bytes with no feature extractors or other network special casing.

the following questions: How can we build models that scale linearly with the length of the sequence? How can we train deeper networks with the same computational and memory budget? Can we use self attention to build generative models that can generate samples with long term coherence?
the question: can attention mechanisms be used for modeling very long range dependencies?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper presents a novel architecture for transformers, and demonstrates its ability to model long sequences.
this paper introduces sparse transformers which are a new class of transformers that are able to model long sequences.
this paper presents a new way to model long sequences with transformers that are much more efficient in memory and computation than previous approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to use the same architecture for a) long sequence modeling, b) deep sequence modeling, c) sparse sequence modeling and d) efficient sequence modeling.
it is now possible to model long range dependencies in sequence data using a single model.
we show that transformers are not just for small sequences and that it is possible to use them for long sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we are able to train deep models with sparse self attention by making a few changes to initialization, training, and architecture, and that the resulting networks can model long range dependencies in data.
sparse factorizations of attention can make it tractable to use attention on sequences of extreme length.
the combination of sparse attention and recomputation allows the use of self-attention on sequences of unprecedented length.
